posts.name: Timebeing
posts.cooked:
I played ground pound with Mars base self destruct sequence out. According to the rules if you skip a turn you skip every phase of that turn, which would also mean the start of the turn when ground pound would be destroyed. So I could skip my turn every turn and heros would never take damage? 

 

Wanted to see if we just got a lucky combo or we miss something in the rules.

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
It depends.

Any start of turn and end of turn effects happen in the order they were played, so if Self-Destruct Sequence came out and then Haka played Ground Pound you choose whether or not to skip your turn for SDS and if you don't you go on to look at any other start of turn effects.

If Ground Pound is played first and then SDS comes out, you destroy Ground Pound first and then get to decide if you want to skip your turn for SDS, not as beneficial that way around.

 

Things can still mess up your plans, villains can destroy ongoing or environment cards, which would stop your choice, Environments can also do this (though not in Wagner Mars Base IIRC) or other heroes might destroy the Environment, also Haka might decide that skipping their turn every round is boring and stop doing it. Just because it's good for the team doesn't mean you have to do it, the primary rule here is "Have fun saving the Multiverse".

 

Welcome to the forums Timebeing, are you the same timebeing that steals all my stuff in RPGs?

On another forum:

That reminds me of a D&D monster called the Time Being. No matter where you are, he can hear you if you mention his name, and he graciously accepts all gifts. If you say "Let's leave this here for the Time Being", he comes along and takes it.

Actually, I believe this was previously discussed with other cards.

Short version: You will always lose Ground Pound - timing is irrelevant.

Long version: Start of turn triggers take effect, then start of turn decisions are made. In this case, the Ground Pound is destroyed at start of turn, then you decide if you want to skip the rest of your turn. I have to have a start of turn phase and Ground Pound goes away at that point.

Anyone else remember that conversation? ![](upload://dZUMDBWc2aavrmlv0dSHsoxpdx6.gif) Or am I just wrong? ![](upload://5c6IsiKf6Y9krcpaRZ8UYyVk8qA.gif)

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
If we look at Spiff's clarifications document we get

but what about your start-of-turn phase? in most cases, cards will say “at the 
start of your turn, you may skip the rest of your turn to do xyz”. because 
start-of-turn effects are activated in the order in which they were played, if 
you have other cards with start-of-turn effects which were in play before the 
card which is causing you to skip the rest of your turn, those start-of-turn 
effects will happen first, then you’ll skip everything else.[br] 
[br]
And as we all know Spiff doesn't put anything in there not clarified by a voice from on high.
I'm sure if we really wanted to we could find the original post so Spiff could add that to his documentation, which might be a good project for us all to contribute to.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: My understanding of Start Phase actions is as has been stated above - they occur in the order in which they were played. So if Omni-10 managed to put out all his components and then Mars played the Self-Destruct Sequence, at the start of his turn Omni-10 would be able to have all his components do their stuff (in the order they entered play) and then decide if he wanted to skip his turn to add to the countdown. Even better if he has a Bio-Engineering Beam handy, of course ;).
